metrics.basis: model_time_ms: sum of the scenario's model-call latencies; wall_ms: scenario start to finish (database and tool time included); per_call: individual planning_eval model calls. Groups: all and expect_plan/expect_stop (by the scenario's expect_plan); check-only scenarios are in no group. Aggregates compare only within the same scenario set; compare same-named scenarios across different sets. Outcomes (first and final pass rate, retries) are over new plans only; revisions (the judged turn ran the revise step) have their own pass rate, locked dishes removed (target 0), dishes changed and model calls per revise turn (turn_model_calls: that turn's calls only; with a button after a follow-up revision, that revision's calls, earlier_revise_calls, count as a revise turn too). Route accuracy is reported for follow-ups (route_as_expected) and first messages apart. Deferred scenarios (deferred_to) are left out of every rate and as_expected, and counted in `deferred`; their cost, calls, tokens and latency count. as_expected_by_role: the same as_expected per scenario-file role (development, regression, held-out), so a regression set never counts toward the held-out rate. replies (over every scenario, deferred included): zero_dishes_shown (a reply or unmet text says the plan has 0 dishes; target 0), wish_unmet_not_said (expect_wish_unmet true but no code-written sign; target 0), buttons (as expected after a next-action button, deferred left out), fallbacks (attempts whose dishes code picked because the planner gave no answer) and fallback_scenarios. Plan 3b-2: a revision is a turn of the change path (reader, frame, picker; its run records `revision`), and its pass rate is the share that made a new version. two_layers: must_violations (what must never be wrong, over every scenario, deferred included; target 0) and must_violation_scenarios; unnecessary_questions over change_allowed_follow_ups (rated follow-ups whose keys accept a change; a follow-up that ended with a question other than the empty-plan and the which-dish question), with unnecessary_question_rate (target at most 0.2). change_path: reader_calls, picker_calls (each picker model call), picker_attempts and frame_ignored over every run of every scenario; an "other" reply's reader call, which no run records, is counted from the turn. must_violations counts must lines (one fault gives one line where cheap: a locked dish removed is said by the locked check only, and the allowed-changes findings share one line); must_violation_scenarios counts scenarios. Only the judged turn is must-checked: with button_after, the follow-up before the button is not (its shown texts are, as every shown text of the thread is).
